Violation ID: 987239
Permit API: 131-20288
Unconventional: Yes
County: Wyoming
Municipality: Windham Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/03/2023
Comments: At time of inspection, 37 degs. and cloudy. There are (4) wells on this pad. They are the Rosalie N WYO 1H, S WYO 1H, N WYO 3H and Jack WYO 8H, all were in production. The (9x5) and the (13x9) annulus vents are plumbed to surface w/ 2" pipe and tied into a 2" common pipe venting to the prod. tanks. All annulus vents are open. ** The Rosalie N WYO 3H has water in the cellar with some bubbling occurring. An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal. 2/10/23) detected 100% LEL and 8% CH4 @ bubbling area. The Operators rep. (Eric Haskins) was called @ 11:30, there was no answer. Message was left describing bubbling in cellar and a request was left to contact OGI (Eric Miller). ** I received an e-mail from Operator @ 15:33 on (3/3/23) stating a lease operator was on site and bubbling has stopped. The cellars of the other wells had water in them w/ no active bubbling observed during insp.. The ALTAIR5X gas meter (cal. 2/10/23) was used at well heads and left on during walk around pad and prod. equipment. No gas was detected in ambient air. - Individual well pressures listed below were all taken off digital SCADA gauges. - Rosalie N WYO 1H - prod. tree top press.: 513 psi., prod. csg. press.: 591 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 8 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 10.1 psi., and prod. line press.: 489.4 psi. - Rosalie N WYO 3H - prod. tree top press.: 515 psi., prod. csg. press.: 614 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 7.9 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 9 psi., and prod. line press.: 497.4 psi. - Rosalie S WYO 1H - prod. tree top press.: 502 psi., prod. csg. press.: 552 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 9 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 9 psi., and prod. line press.: 494 psi. - Jack WYO 8H - prod. tree top press.: 507 psi., prod. csg. press.: 554 psi., (9x5) annulus press.: 9 psi, (13x9) annulus press.: 9 psi., and prod. line press.: 499 psi. - There is an on site compressor, running at time of inspection. - There is self contained ancillary equipment on pad. - There are (2) open well slots on the pad. - No other obvious concerns or additional violations noted.

I observed the release area during the inspection and conducted field screen readings for conductivity in the release area. Soil conductivity screening was conducted in the excavated release area. Conductivity field screenings were conducted on the impacted soils; readings ranged from 0.15-0.32 mS/cm. Violations noted. Please note that the cited violations were immediately corrected by the operator after the released occurred.

Comments: On 5/30/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Stoorza well site. It was 74 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. PCSM is addressed by three retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.There were two wells staged for production. Both wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The GPUs and production tank had secondary containment. A gas compressor is on site but was not running during the inspection.An inspection conducted by the department on 3/30/2023 described three waste piles of excavated material transported from the Chesapeake Grippo well site that had been temporarily stored at this location. These three piles have been removed from the Stoorza well site location along with the secondary containment structures. I viewed the areas of the pad surface and did not witness visible evidence of contamination. Due to the dry conditions in these locations, I could not screen the areas for conductance during this inspection.No violations were noted during this inspection.Violations are still outstanding for inspection IDs 3524618 and 3537962 for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface in proximity to stockpiles of contaminated excavated waste. Laboratory analysis determined the fluid contained high levels of barium, strontium and chlorides.I left the site at 1130 hours.

Comments: I received a call from Tighe Truman of Seneca Resources on Monday July 22, 2024, informing me of a release of produced water on the E08-L pad. He said the produced water line had a hole it it, and they initially thought it was going to be a non-reportable amount. Upon excavation of the soil at the site of the release, they realized it was more than they initially thought. We made arrangements to meet onsite the following day.At the time of this inspection a small (10'x 10') area had been dug out to a depth of 6-7'. It is estimated that 20 gallons of produced water was released to the ground. Conductivity readings in the excavated area were near background levels. The produced water had stayed in a small area and there is no indication of further contamination at this time. The failed plastic line was already repaired at the time of this inspection. The excavated soil is being stored onsite inside a temporary containment dike. Pending laboratory analysis the soil will be hauled to an approved waste facility.

Comments: On 2/28/20 at 1250 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Diversified Production, LLC's J Budd Overman 5 well (API 063-35887) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. in response to a reported release of approximately 30 gallons of production fluid from a tank located onsite. The release occured on 2/25/20 and was immediately reported to the Department. The release primarily stayed within the secondary containment, with some material making it to an adjacent agricultural field. The operator reported that the tank may have been compromised by a small caliber projectile or shot pellet, which caused the release. The tank was not located onsite at the time of my inspection. The operator stated the tank was pumped out and taken to the shop for repairs. The release of production fluids from a tank onto the ground constitutes violations of SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1), and 78.57(a). The violations will be resolved upon remediation of the impacted area, temporary stabilization of the well site, and submission of disposal receipts to the Department.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 1/02/2025
Violation Code: OGA3216(D) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - ITEMS RELATED TO PRODUCTION OR STORAGE - Failure to remove production/storage facilities, supplies and equipment and restore the well site within 9 months of plugging a well.
Violation ID: 8212800
Permit API: 129-23976
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/02/2025
Comments: On January 2, 2025 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of the Louis Yemc 1 plugged well site located in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3863980 where violations were continued for failure to restore the well site.At the time of this inspection, the access road, which was approved to remain existing (documented in IR 3862939) was observed with no erosion or sedimentation issues. During IR 3863980, the Department observed the plugged well site to be exhibiting close to 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth everywhere except for a pit that had recently been dug for the removal of the pit contents. At the time of this inspection all of the plugged well site including the area where the pit was dug appears to be exhibiting close to 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth.During IR 3863980, compost filter sock (CFS) was observed downslope of the pit to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues. Plugging operations was completed on 12/08/2023 (according to Department records), therefore the site should have been restored no later than 9/08/2024. The well site restoration report shall be issued within 60 days after restoration of the well site in accordance with 78.65(3). At the time of this inspection, the CFS was still observed to be installed, a frozen puddle of water was observed in front of and behind the CFS, however, no erosion or sedimentation issues was observed beyond this frozen puddle. The Department recommends the operator further stabilize the plugged well site to minimize the pooling of fluid in this area to prevent future erosion and sedimentation issues from occurring.A pipe was observed laying on the ground within the plugged well site, the Department recommends the Operator remove all equipment from the well site. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for failure to restore the well site shall remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: This Inspection is being conducted in response to a complaint that was received by the Department on 12/11/2019 regarding concerns about large rusted holes in the sides of several brine tanks. WQS Eric Norman is assisting. The conditions during this inspection are cloudy in the mid 50's. An Act 9 Sign is at the entrance but is very faded. The Department recommends that the Operator maintain the sign to regulated specifications. The ERP and SDS are on site, the ERP appears to be site specific. The access road appears to be built, with no visible signs of accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The well head is labeled. No leaks or discharges observed. The site appears to be constructed and the well appears equipped for production. Associated production equipment and Production Tanks are on site. The Production Tanks are in an earthen dike. The earthen dike appears to have some holes, possibly associated with nuisance wildlife, the Department recommends that the operator take steps to correct those issues in order to maintain the structural integrity of the earthen dike. The Production Tanks appear to be in poor condition with large holes in both tanks toward the top of both. The Tank closest to the well head appears to have corrosion over most of the tank. No leaks, spills, or distressed vegetation is observed. Inspections 2716702, 2819306, and 2856714 mentioned issues with corrosion and holes in these brine tanks dating back to 04/10/2018. The Department is requesting monthly inspection logs for the Production Tanks from 04/10/2018 until 12/30/2019. The Department is also requesting a time table for correcting or removing these tanks. Based on this inspection, violations are being issued. More violations may be issued based on operator response to the NOV's.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's (Blackhill) Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/10/2023 at 1525 hours. The weather was 67 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted to evaluate remedial activities that were conducted after a release that occurred on 4/6/2023.Moody and Associates Inc. (Moody's)(Environmental consultant) was onsite during my inspection and have been conducting field screenings for Blackhill. Since the release that occurred on 4/6/2023, Blackhill has had the entire southern stormwater conveyance channel excavated (photos #2, 3 and 4). Blackhill reported that soil readings in the channel were now field measured below 1.0mS/cm. Excavation points on both sides of the access road culvert are now acting as sumps for the collection of residual fluids. A water truck was stationed at these points today, recovering any collected fluids. The pad surface area that was determined to be impacted by the release has been excavated as much as possible (photos #6 and 7). Blackhill explained that collected fluids shown in photo #7 are also being recovered. Fluid in this area, which is located right next to the initial release point, was field measured at ~17.8mS/cm today. Blackhill reported that equipment will be brought in on either 4/11/2023 or 4/12/2023 to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment structure in order to excavate beneath them. The impacted stormwater basin has been emptied to where just a few puddles remain (photo #1). All water collected from the basin was stored in tanks shown in photo #9 and continues to be trucked offsite for disposal or reuse. I field measured a small puddle near the stormwater channel entry point of the basin which returned a reading of ~1.75mS/cm. All impacted materials that have been recovered are stored in lined and covered waste containers which are held on secondary containment (photo #8). All violations associated with the releases from 1/2/2023 and from 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time against API #015-23733. I departed the site at 1620 hours.As a follow-up to the violations cited on 4/6/2023, the DEP requests a summary of the quantity of fluids collected in regards to the produced water release, including the stormwater basin, and where the water was transported after collection. This information can be provided in the NOV response.

Inspection Date: 3/04/2021
Comments: On 03/04/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone conducted a follow-up inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s (CALLC) STONE location. The purpose of this inspection was to document the status of the site and visually observe the location of a previous release of production / flowback fluids. Details regarding the release can be found within inspection report (IR) # 3141162 & 3144646. I arrived at 1232 hours. The weather was 31 degrees with overcast skies. Slopes around the site had approximately 2 – 4 inches of snow cover present. Majority of the pad surface had puddles present. At the time of this inspection, there were 2 roll-off containers labelled as "BRINE" stationed within a shared secondary containment (photo # 2). The release detailed in IR # 3141162 appears to have occurred west of the currently stationed roll-off containers, based on photos within the report. Puddles on the pad surface around the roll-off containers’ secondary containment was screened for field measured specific conductivity using an OAKTON PCTS 50 meter. Puddles immediately adjacent to the western edge of the containment ranged from 1010 uS/cm – 2.56 mS/cm (photo # 4, 6, 8). Higher readings appeared to trend off the NW corner of the containment. Fluid within containment was screened at 14.88 mS/cm (photo # 14). A visual inspection of the containment did not reveal any obvious deficiencies. I called Eric Hottenstein (CALLC, HSE Supervisor) at 1313 hours in order to discuss my findings. Mr. Hottenstein stated a vacuum truck would be sent out in order to vacuum the pad and CALLC would investigate the origin of the cause of the elevated conductivity readings. Violations cited within IR # 3141162 remain in the outstanding status against well permit # 015-23632. I departed the site at 1330 hours.

Comments: This is a producing combination well with a gas powered pumpjack attached. The well is plumbed to a 210 barrel stock tank and 50 barrel poly tank on site. It appears as though there has been a leak on this site recently. There is an area approximately 10x20 feet with staining of soil and dead vegetation, along with a finger of oil stained soil in an erosion rill about 20 feet further. By the end of the day on 8/23, the operator had the site cleaned up and seeded and mulched. No further inspection of this site will be necessary at this time.

Comments: On November 26 2024, the Department conducted a routine partial inspection of the Mamont 16 Well Pad (ESCGP-3 issued on 11/30/2021 and expires on 11/29/2026) in regards to a referral from Environmental Protection Specialist (EPS) Zane Shaffer regarding an apparent spill observed outside of secondary containment. Present during today's inspection is Zane Shaffer (DEP) and Justin Ruth (CNX). The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared to be stabilized. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. The Act 9 sign was present at the time of the inspection, and appeared to be in good condition. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, site plans, and Safety Data Sheets (SDS), were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of the inspection the operator was currently drilling the K well. No waterways are reported to have been impacted and remediation was ongoing during the time of IR 3969681.Prior to conducting this inspection, the Department spoke via phone with Range Resources representative Nate Smiell who explained that remediation was completed and confirmation samples were collected in the impacted area, per the cleanup requirements of Act 2.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Some minor potholes were observed in the access road (see photo 2). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 3). There are six additional wells onsite that also appear to be in production (see photo 5). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 8). Secondary containment has been installed onsite in location of the GPU units (see photo 10). A crane is onsite to move the GPU units into the newly-installed secondary containment (see photos 9 and 11). This is being conducted per the requirements of an active Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) between the operator and the Department. The rolloff boxes that were present during the time of IR 3969681 appear to have been removed from site. No visual evidence of any remaining impacted material was observed in the formerly impacted area.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that visual remediation of the impacted area has been successfully completed. However, violations issued from IR 3969681 shall remain outstanding, as the NOI to Remediation of this release under Act 2 requirements have not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB Program at the time of this inspection.
